results.title: Mixed Sources of Pb and Sn in late Bronze Age European tin ingots provide insights into production processes - ScienceDirect
results.content:
Title: Mixed Sources of Pb and Sn in late Bronze Age European tin ingots provide insights into production processes - ScienceDirect
# Mixed Sources of Pb and Sn in late Bronze Age European tin ingots provide insights into production processes. Multi-element mixing trends are evident in tin ingots from Late Bronze Age shipwrecks of Uluburun and the Israeli coast. Tin ingots have been the focus of multi-method studies involving Sn and Pb isotopes, as well as trace element patterns, in an effort to determine provenance. Given the apparent extent of mixing evident in tin ingots, mixed metal sources must be considered when interpreting the isotopic and trace element compositions of tin artifacts to infer the metal's provenance. However, recently it has been recognized that geologically young (<500 Ma) cassiterite typically contains only a few ppm of Pb, and that the Pb content of most of the prehistoric tin ingots that have been excavated from Europe and Africa exceeds that which could have acquired from cassiterite alone, the excess Pb having been acquired from contaminant minerals in ore concentrates, intentional addition of Pb metal, or unintentional contamination during the casting or smelting process (Powell et al., 2021, 2024). Thus, mixed metal compositions are the norm for tin ingots, at least with respect to Pb. Given that the presence of Pb from sources other than cassiterite is nearly ubiquitous in tin artifacts, we undertook a re-examination of the isotopic and trace element composition from the corpus of articles concerning Late Bronze Age European tin ingots. This study re-examines the Bronze Age tin ingots excavated within the European region based on heritage analyses of Sn isotopes, Pb isotopes, and trace elements. Given that it has been demonstrated that Pb contamination is widespread in tin metal (Powell et al., 2024), and that both Pb concentration and Pb isotope composition are frequently used in provenance studies, herein we focus initially on Pb in our mixing analysis, before investigating Sn and trace elements. ### The Salcombe metal cargoes: new light on the provenance and circulation of tin and copper in Later Bronze Age Europe provided by trace elements and isotopes.

results.title: Understand Your Product’s Origin | Advanced Isotopic Analysis
results.content: ### **Origin through isotopes**. #### We offer innovative isotope analysis, helping you to fully understand and validate the origin of your products, as well as providing strategic data on traceability to help addressing environmental issues. The intrinsic isotopic signatures of your product can be used to trace its primary origin and also authenticate the specific processes applied to your products. Thanks to this isotopic signature, we are able to determine with high precision and accuracy the origin, age and/or processes undergone by an element. The natural isotopic compositions of a product are the results of different external parameters, such as its primary origin and the physical, chemical or biological processes that affect it. The team here at Advanced Isotopic Analysis has a specific expertise with heavy elements - particularly Mercury (Hg). Prior to isotopic analysis, it is first necessary to determine the precise concentration of the targeted element. Our team is able to deliver quantitative trace element analysis, which can also be used as a complementary tool to characterize processes and origins.
